title: Urea 46% N Fertilizer
description: Prilled and granular urea (46-0-0) — the most concentrated solid nitrogen fertilizer, supplied to date palm, vegetable, and cereal growers across Oman.

details.longDescription:
Urea (CO(NH2)2, CAS 57-13-6) at 46% nitrogen is the most concentrated solid nitrogen fertilizer available and the main nitrogen source across Oman's agriculture: date palm plantations in Al Batinah and Al Dakhiliyah, vegetable farms, greenhouses and cereal and forage cropping. Global Chemicals LLC supplies IFDC-standard prilled urea (1–2.4 mm) and granular urea (2–4 mm) from stock in Muscat in 25 kg PP bags and 1,000 kg big bags, with biuret below 1.0% and moisture below 0.5%.

Which form to order depends on how it is applied. Prilled urea dissolves fastest and suits fertigation through drip systems and foliar sprays; granular urea spreads evenly from broadcast spreaders and blends with other granular fertilizers without segregating. The biuret limit matters most for foliar use: biuret is phytotoxic to leaves, so a 0.5–1.0% foliar solution should be made only from low-biuret product. Typical date palm programmes apply 150–300 kg of urea per hectare per season, split into several doses from late winter through fruit development rather than one heavy application.

In Oman's alkaline calcareous soils (pH 7.5–8.5), urea left on the surface hydrolyses to ammonium and loses a large share of its nitrogen as ammonia gas. Incorporate it or water it in the same day, or deliver it through fertigation, where the loss is small. In drip systems urea dissolves completely and endothermically, so the stock tank cools noticeably; mix in batches and let it reach ambient temperature before injection.

Urea is hygroscopic. Keep bags closed, off the floor and out of direct sun; once opened in humid coastal air it cakes within days. Do not dry-blend urea with calcium nitrate or ammonium nitrate: the mixture absorbs moisture and turns to slurry in storage. Beyond the farm, the same product is the feedstock for urea-formaldehyde and melamine resins; automotive-grade urea for diesel exhaust fluid is a different specification, so ask before ordering for that use.

title: Diammonium Phosphate (DAP 18-46-0)
description: Granular DAP fertilizer — 18% nitrogen, 46% phosphate — the highest-analysis phosphorus fertilizer for base dressing across Omani farms.

details.longDescription:
Diammonium Phosphate (DAP, 18-46-0) is the world's most widely used phosphorus fertilizer and the primary base-dressing product across Oman. Supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in granular form, DAP delivers 18% nitrogen and 46% P2O5 in a single application — ideal for pre-planting incorporation for vegetables, alfalfa, and date palm root feeding. Fully water-soluble in the root zone and compatible with most nitrogen and potassium fertilizers for custom blending.

In Oman's calcareous soils, phosphate is quickly fixed by calcium, so DAP works best placed in a band near the root zone rather than broadcast on the surface. Keep it out of direct contact with seed, because the ammonium released on dissolution can injure germinating seedlings. DAP is not the right choice for drip lines: its solution is mildly alkaline and it precipitates with calcium in hard irrigation water. Use MAP or a water-soluble NPK for fertigation, and never put DAP in the same stock tank as calcium nitrate.

For custom blending, the 2–4 mm granule matches granular urea and granular MOP, which keeps blends from segregating in transport. description: Compound and custom-blended NPK fertilizers — 20-20-20, 19-19-19, 15-15-15 and tailored ratios for Oman's date palm, vegetable, and greenhouse growers.

details.longDescription:
Global Chemicals LLC supplies water-soluble and granular NPK compound fertilizers to farms and greenhouses across Oman — including the standard 20-20-20, 19-19-19, 15-15-15 grades and custom-blended ratios matched to soil analysis and crop stage. Water-soluble grades are formulated for drip fertigation with full solubility, low insolubles (<0.1%), and micronutrient supplementation options (chelated Fe, Mn, Zn, B, Cu, Mo). Granular grades serve conventional broadcast and side-dressing applications for date palm, alfalfa, and open-field vegetables.

Choose the ratio by crop stage. Balanced grades such as 20-20-20 and 19-19-19 suit establishment and vegetative growth; high-potassium grades such as 15-5-30 and 12-12-36 support flowering, fruit fill and colour. Where irrigation water is hard, as in much of Oman, keep calcium in a separate stock tank from phosphate- and sulphate-bearing NPK, and flush drip lines with acidified water periodically to prevent emitter scaling.

Custom blends are built from your soil and water analysis, with micronutrients added as chelates so they stay available at high pH. title: Potassium Chloride (MOP 60% K2O)
description: Muriate of Potash (MOP) — 60% K2O potassium chloride fertilizer for date palms, fruit trees, and field crops across Oman.

details.longDescription:
Muriate of Potash (MOP / potassium chloride, 60% K2O) is the most widely used potassium fertilizer in Oman — critical for date palm fruit sizing, quality, and post-harvest storage life, and for tolerance to Oman's saline groundwater. Supplied in standard and granular grades, MOP is applied by broadcast, banding, or fertigation (standard grade fully soluble). Global Chemicals LLC also supplies Sulphate of Potash (SOP, 50% K2O) for chloride-sensitive crops on request.

MOP supplies potassium at the lowest cost per unit of K2O, but it also adds chloride. Where the irrigation water is already saline, or for chloride-sensitive crops such as citrus, avocado, strawberries and some vegetables, Sulphate of Potash is the safer choice, and we supply it on request. Granular MOP (2–4 mm) is sized to blend with DAP and granular urea without segregation; the fine standard grade dissolves fully for fertigation.

MOP is stable in storage and is not hygroscopic under normal conditions, but keep it dry to prevent caking in big bags. title: Calcium Nitrate Fertilizer
description: Water-soluble calcium nitrate — 15.5% N, 26.5% CaO — the standard calcium and nitrate-nitrogen source for fertigation of tomatoes, cucumbers, and greenhouse crops.

details.longDescription:
Calcium Nitrate (15.5% N, 26.5% CaO) is the standard calcium fertilizer for greenhouse and open-field horticulture across Oman — essential for preventing blossom-end rot in tomatoes and peppers, tip-burn in lettuce, and bitter pit in fruit. As the only widely-available calcium source fully compatible with fertigation, it dissolves clearly, delivers nitrate-nitrogen (preferred over ammonium in high-pH substrates), and supports strong cell wall structure. Supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in 25 kg bags for greenhouse growers in Nizwa, Barka, and across Al Batinah.

Calcium nitrate must go in its own stock tank (the "A" tank in a two-tank fertigation system). Concentrated with phosphates it forms insoluble calcium phosphate, and with sulphates it forms gypsum, either of which blocks drip emitters. Inject the A and B tanks separately and let them meet only in the dilute irrigation line.

The product is hygroscopic and will liquefy in humid air, so keep bags sealed and stored indoors. For foliar calcium on fruit, spray in the early morning or evening at low concentration and avoid midday heat. title: Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate (33% Zn) — Agricultural
description: Micronutrient zinc sulphate — 33% Zn monohydrate — for correcting zinc deficiency in Oman's alkaline soils, date palm, and greenhouse crops.

details.longDescription:
Zinc deficiency is one of the most widespread micronutrient problems in Oman's alkaline calcareous soils — reducing yield in date palm, citrus, vegetables, and forage. Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate (33% Zn) is the standard soil and foliar correction. Global Chemicals LLC supplies agricultural-grade ZSM for soil broadcast (20–40 kg/ha), fertigation, and foliar sprays (0.2–0.5% solution). Chelated zinc EDTA also available for high-pH conditions where sulphate fixation is a concern.

Zinc sulphate should not be tank-mixed with phosphate fertilizers, which precipitate zinc phosphate and take the zinc out of reach of the plant. On very high-pH soils a soil application can be partly fixed within weeks, which is why foliar sprays and chelated zinc are often used alongside it. Spray foliar zinc in the early morning or evening to avoid leaf scorch, and confirm the need with a leaf or soil test before repeating applications.

title: Agricultural Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate)
description: Agricultural-grade gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) for sodic soil reclamation, calcium supply, and structure improvement across Oman's irrigated farmland.

details.longDescription:
Agricultural gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate (CaSO4·2H2O, CAS 10101-41-4), mined and ground to below 2 mm, with 85% minimum purity, 23% calcium and 18% sulphur. It is the standard amendment for reclaiming sodic and saline-sodic soils across Oman's irrigated regions, where saline groundwater raises exchangeable sodium, disperses clay and destroys soil structure and infiltration. Gypsum supplies soluble calcium that displaces sodium from the cation exchange complex, so the soil re-aggregates and water moves through it again. It is also a non-acidifying calcium and sulphur source for peanuts, alfalfa and forage crops. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 25 kg bags, 1,000 kg big bags and bulk.

How much to apply. The dose depends on the exchangeable sodium percentage and the cation exchange capacity, which only a soil test gives; a working rule is about 1.7 tonnes of gypsum per hectare for every milliequivalent of exchangeable sodium per 100 g of soil to be replaced in the top 15 cm, which is why field rates run from 2 to 10 t/ha. Gypsum dissolves slowly (roughly 2.5 g/L), so the fine grind matters: finer particles react faster. Reclamation only works if the displaced sodium is leached out, so spread the gypsum before an irrigation that drains below the root zone and plan follow-up leaching with the best-quality water available.

Gypsum can also be dissolved in irrigation water to raise its calcium and lower its sodium adsorption ratio before it reaches the soil, which protects infiltration on drip and sprinkler schemes fed from brackish wells. Because it does not change soil pH and does not burn foliage, it can be applied to standing date palm, vegetables and forage without a withdrawal period, and it can be blended with most fertilizers except those that react with calcium, such as phosphates.

Store bags dry; the product is not hazardous and needs no special handling beyond dust control. title: Humic Acid (Leonardite Extract)
description: Water-soluble humic and fulvic acids — leonardite-derived soil conditioner that improves nutrient uptake, soil structure, and root growth in Oman's low-organic desert soils.

details.longDescription:
Humic acid (leonardite-derived potassium humate) is a powerful soil conditioner for Oman's low-organic-matter desert and irrigated soils. Boosts cation exchange capacity, chelates and mobilises phosphorus and micronutrients (particularly Fe and Zn), improves soil aggregate structure, and stimulates root growth. Compatible with drip fertigation and foliar sprays. Global Chemicals LLC supplies water-soluble flake and powder forms (65–75% humic acid) — ideal for regenerative fertilization programs on date palm, vegetables, and turf.

Dissolve humic acid in water before adding other fertilizers. It can flocculate in acidic solutions and in very hard water, so do not premix it with acids or concentrated calcium, and run a small jar test with your own irrigation water before filling the tank. In drip programmes it works best in small, frequent doses through the season rather than one large application, alongside a normal NPK programme rather than replacing it.
